$comment: A SECOND NAME OF A DEFINITION (P69, lane cs): the GNU `alias("target")` attribute, compiled. Each alias is one more symbol row on its target's definition (the shape every object reader makes of a foreign alias), and the unit refers to an external alias by NAME, so a call, a read, a write and an address taken through it are the target's: an external alias of a function (called through a volatile pointer so the address compare is a runtime one), a weak one nothing replaces, an external alias of an object written through, a module-private alias (its uses bound to the target by the semantic tier), a GLOBAL alias of a `static` body (return 7: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 on x86_64 Linux and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 build and run that pair at -O0 and -O2, MEASURED by lane cs's probe al2 cell 3; the PE writer refused it until P69 gave the alias a record of its own), and an alias of a TENTATIVE definition, which makes it a definition of the unit, never a common. Every return before 42 names the first fact that failed. No Mach-O target: every Apple clang refuses an alias, and the Mach-O documents refuse it by name (`symbolAliasUnsupportedReason`). The `release` arm pins that dead-code removal keeps every definition an alias names (DCE roots each target) and that the optimizer carries the aliases through every rebuild.
